title: How cheap AI is made: distillation
label: AI EXPLAINED

yt.title: Under 30 minutes, under ₹5,000
notes: Under 30 minutes, under ₹5,000 (under $50) of rented GPUs
Beat OpenAI's o1-preview (2024) on competition maths (researchers' report)
Its teacher: a smarter AI. That's distillation

lines.text: Under thirty minutes. Under five thousand rupees. [1] That's what it took to make an existing AI beat an early OpenAI reasoning model at maths, its researchers say. [2] Its teacher? [3] A smarter AI. This is called distillation.

yt.title: A big AI teaches a small one
notes: Teacher: big, slow, expensive
Student: small and fast

lines.text: The idea: [1] a big, slow, expensive AI [2] teaches a small, fast one.

yt.title: More than the final answer
notes: An answer key only says 'cat'
The teacher gives 90% cat, 9% tiger, 1% car
Chatbots do this with words: how the teacher weighs every next word

lines.text: An answer key just says 'cat', [1] but a teacher AI shows how much it looks like each option: [2] ninety percent cat, nine percent tiger, one percent car. [3] Those small numbers are hidden lessons. [4] Chatbots learn the same way, with words: the student copies how the teacher weighs every next word.

yt.title: It copied written answers
notes: Not the teacher's percentages: written answers
1,000 solved examples from a smarter AI, on an already-trained open model (s1, 2025)
The ₹5,000 paid only for this last step
Copying answers counts as distillation too

lines.text: And that maths model? It didn't copy the teacher's percentages. [1] Researchers gave an already-trained open model one thousand solved examples, written by a smarter AI. [2] The five thousand rupees paid only for this last step. [3] Learning from written answers counts as distillation too.

yt.title: Copied mistakes, and the rules
notes: The student copies the teacher's mistakes
Big AI companies' terms ban training a rival on their answers

lines.text: The catch: [1] the student copies its teacher's mistakes too. [2] And most big AI companies' terms ban using their answers to build a rival.

yt.title: Small first, bigger when it slips
notes: Emails, summaries, data: a small model (Flash, Flash-Lite, mini)
Multi-step, or it keeps getting it wrong: a bigger model like Gemini Pro (usually paid)
Developers: Pro ≈ 3x Flash per use (Google API, Oct 2026)
Test 20 real emails on the small one first

lines.text: So which do you use? [1] Emails, summaries, pulling out data: a small model is enough, like Flash, Flash-Lite or mini. [2] Multi-step tasks, or an Excel formula the small one keeps getting wrong? Move up to a bigger model, like Gemini Pro, usually a paid plan. [3] For developers paying per use, Pro costs about three times Flash right now. [4] So test twenty of your real emails on the small one first.
